summary: This bill amends the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to lower the minimum percentage of identified students required for schools in high-poverty areas to offer universal free meals to 25 percent, starting July 1, 2025.

scores.thoughts: This bill expands eligibility for universal meal service in schools, which would likely increase federal expenditures related to the National School Lunch Act. The primary purpose of the bill is to lower the threshold for this service, directly implying increased spending.

By lowering the threshold for universal meal service in high-poverty areas, the bill expands access to a key social safety net program for children, ensuring more students receive meals regardless of individual application status.
